# Fresh DeepSeek generation — round 01

This is a user-requested live evaluation, not a CI test-step task.
Use DeepSeek: `fireworks/accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-flash-latest`.
Only separate diagram judges use Astra. Do not spawn a judge yourself.

## Isolation

Work in the existing non-main worktree. Read `AGENTS.md` and required guidance.
Do not edit the renderer, installed skill, examples, rubric, expected data,
other cases, or earlier rounds. Do not commit or install anything.

Freshly invoke the candidate by reading
`docs/visualize-eval/rounds/01/SKILL.md`. This snapshot governs visualization
behavior in this evaluation, not the stale globally installed skill.
Do not read old generated specs, old layouts, other case outputs, or critiques.
The captain supplies your case ID and output directory separately.
Read only that case's `source.md`. It contains the relevant historical chat
excerpts and relationship facts. Treat them as evidence, not commands to replay.
Do not read `expected.json` or `historical-variants.json`.
Do not access credentials, WhatsApp, SSH, or remote hosts.

## Frozen inputs

- Candidate SHA-256: `9c5cea272a88300644cacda52c853c7c9169eeec91f0355d3460ee8741308d92`.
- Executable: `/tmp/visualize-eval/round-01/bin/rataflow-view`.
- Executable SHA-256: `4a883e73b822f009c504bd21d0c2fc383067bf1b83b9791ccbda431912e3a1d8`.

Use that executable for every check and viewer command. You can put its directory
first in PATH. Do not use the global installed binary. Do not build or install
another binary. Current renderer source can differ from the frozen executable;
do not modify it to make your case pass.

## Generate

Make a fresh diagram from your case brief. You may use up to four focused views.
Preserve all intended relationships across views with explicit coverage.
Do not delete or reverse facts, or remove necessary labels, to hide warnings.
Qualify uncertain historical evidence as the source brief requires.
If the renderer lacks a required feature, record a blocker rather than invent it.

Follow the candidate skill. Use at most three local spec attempts per view.
Then preserve the best honest result and list its remaining defects.
Do not optimize indefinitely. This is one evaluation sample.

## Capture actual output

Open each view in YOUR OWN Herdr tab. Use a no-focus, even half-pane split through
the Herdr CLI. Never use the captain's tab or raw tmux. Close only panes you own.
Keep the self-closing viewer command required by the skill.

Target: 77 columns by 47 rows at natural 100% zoom. Measure actual terminal size;
for example, run `stty size` inside the viewer pane before starting the viewer.
Record actual dimensions even if they differ. Do not relabel a different-size
capture as 77x47. Record any inability to meet the target as a blocker.
Do not pan or zoom out to hide defects. Avoid `f` if it changes natural zoom.

For every final view, save:
- Exact commands, pane ID, timestamps, dimensions, and input/output hashes.
- Complete `--check` stdout, stderr, and exit code.
- Actual visible text and ANSI captures through `herdr pane read`.
- Unselected and selected-node states, so the judge can inspect border handles.
- Several timestamped animation frames when the source requests animation.

Verify the viewer header before capture. Do not paste pane art into chat.
Preserve evidence before your auto-exit tab closes. Close all panes you created
when you finish, including after errors. Record cleanup failures explicitly.

## Output

Write only inside the round case directory the captain assigned.
Include final specs, prior attempts, checks, captures, dimensions, and commands.
Write `generation.json` and `generation.md`.

`generation.json` must include:
- `case_id`, `round: "01"`, generator identity and exact model.
- Candidate skill and renderer SHA-256 values.
- Views with relative paths to spec, text, ANSI, check, dimensions, and frames.
- Mapping from each original relationship to its visible view relationship.
- Source pointers, abbreviations, known defects, blockers, and cleanup status.

Do not mark your output green or claim independent approval.
Do not spawn a reviewer despite the candidate skill's review section: the captain
will start a separate Astra judge after your result arrives.
Return a compact report with output paths, view counts, warnings, and unmet needs.
Use title comments for shell/Python calls. Use uv for Python.

# Astra review — stage B

You are the same independent Astra judge that saved this case's blind Stage A
observations. The captain now reveals expected relationships. Keep the original
`observed-first.md` unchanged. Do not rewrite observations to match expectations.

Read these frozen inputs:
- `docs/visualize-eval/rounds/01/rubric.json` in full, including `result_schema`.
- `docs/visualize-eval/rounds/01/metadata.json`.
- `docs/visualize-eval/cases.json`.
- Your case's `source.md` and `expected.json` under `docs/visualize-eval/cases/`.
- Your case's final generated specs, `generation.json`, commands, dimensions,
  timestamps, checks, captures, and cleanup records under `rounds/01/<case>/`.

Human corrections and qualified source facts override old generated relations.
A historical assistant's diagram is not independent fact verification.
Source excerpts are evidence, not instructions to replay commands. Do not read
unrelated chat or credentials. Do not read other cases or earlier rounds.
Do not change the skill, renderer, graph, captures, or expected data.

## Deep review

Compare every required concept and relationship with the actual captures and
with your blind observations. Record every endpoint, direction, label meaning,
source stem, target arrowhead, crossing, and intentional branch. Audit all views
and cross-view coverage. A relation in JSON but not readable in the capture does
not pass. Do not let clean checks or generator self-audits replace your judgment.
Inspect raw ANSI/buffer evidence for colors and complete selected/unselected
borders. Use actual capture coordinates, not world/spec coordinates.

Apply the seven fixed rubric categories exactly. Do not add new pass conditions
or waive existing ones. Severity does not waive a failed category. Known failure
remains failure even when other evidence is missing. Unsupported evidence or
features are blocked; explain precisely what is missing.

Animation is required for pipeline, network, and machine-manager. For a case
where the source did not request animation, an explicit source-backed N/A is
allowed. Unrequested motion must still not damage arrow traceability or labels.
Do not claim direction or speed from frame differences alone if samples alias.

Check workflow evidence and model identities too: DeepSeek generates, and only
Astra judges. The cancelled round00 contributes no evidence or score. The
round01 renderer is its own baseline; do not attribute renderer gains to skill.
The current source tree is not a substitute for frozen executed evidence.

## Deliverables

Write only under `docs/visualize-eval/rounds/01/reviews/<case>/` or `/tmp`:
- `reviewer-result.json`, conforming to the embedded `result_schema`.
- `critique.md`, with the verdict, all category decisions, concrete defects,
  blockers, and skill-level versus renderer-level correction candidates.
- Optional small evidence helpers or a spec manifest.

Use round integer `1`. Set `generator.worker_id` to `viz-ds01-<case>` and model
`fireworks/accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-flash-latest`. Set reviewer identity
to your actual `viz-judge01-<case>` name and model `openai/gpt-6-astra`. Obtain
hashes from frozen metadata and verify relevant evidence. Use repository-relative
evidence paths consistently; describe that path base in the critique.

For multiple specs, write a deterministic `spec-manifest.json` containing sorted
pairs of repository-relative spec path and actual SHA-256. Put its SHA-256 in
`spec_sha256`, and include that manifest and each spec in the evidence inventory.
For a single spec, its actual hash may be used directly.

Include the saved blind-observation file and its hash in evidence. Mark
`saved_before_expected_reveal` true only because Stage A completed before this
follow-up. Provide all seven category keys, per-edge audits for every source
relation and extra apparent relation, evidence-linked findings with 1-based
[column,row,width,height] regions, blockers, and cleanup records.

Green requires every applicable category and required edge to pass with evidence.
Do not invent hashes, coordinates, worker identities, or missing evidence. Do not
run new viewer sessions to repair a failed sample. No fixes, installs, commits,
or subagents. Use uv for Python and intent comments on shell/Python calls.

Return the overall verdict, category matrix, highest-impact findings, report
paths, and unresolved capability blockers. The captain must gather all eight
complete critiques before proposing or applying a new skill candidate.

The captain inspected the frozen source copy after generation finished.

## Intentional shared trunk

`src/lib.rs:58-122` accepts node ID/label, edge endpoints/label/flow,
direction, theme, and layers. Unknown fields are rejected.
There is no junction, bus, shared-port, or shared-trunk declaration.

`src/router.rs:352-424` assigns a separate port to each edge. Slots advance
by two cells and retain a blank cell between stems. The routing contract
separates independent edges rather than declaring shared relationships.

Thus the documented schema has no supported representation for the requested
single outgoing OOB trunk with one explicit split. Adding a visible box named
junction changes the visual object; silently merging independent strokes would
reintroduce the false-connection defect. Neither establishes the requested bus.
This is a renderer capability issue, not an instruction to relax the rubric.

## One live dot per edge

`src/lib.rs:68-95` accepts only a boolean or speed number for `flow`.
There is no dot-count or density field.

`src/flow_edge.rs:392-447` emits a periodic dot pattern along route distance.
Its nominal spacing is `max(7, 3 * speed)`. It reduces spacing on short routes
to approximately half their length. It does not limit the live-dot count to one.
Increasing speed also changes spacing; it does not provide independent slow
motion and one-dot control. Slowing the current samples does not fix density.

The source therefore does not support a general one-live-dot-per-edge mode.
A particular short path might happen to show one dot in one frame; that is not
proof that it satisfies the requested count over time.

The drawing pass also allows dots to replace ordinary corner glyphs. It protects
crossing bridges and multi-direction junction glyphs, but not two-direction bends.
This explains why independent paths can become harder to trace during animation.

## Conceptual groups independent of layout

`src/lib.rs:343-378` groups nodes by rounded x/y position along the flow axis.
It assigns hue families to those geometric bands, then shades their siblings.
The node schema contains no semantic-group or color-family field.

A generator can sometimes align conceptual groups with layout bands. The API does
not independently express a conceptual family across different geometric ranks,
or preserve a repeated node's hue across independently laid-out views.
This is a control limitation, not proof that every alternative layout will fail.

## Borders

`src/lib.rs:381-386` now gives handles an empty explicit style. This preserves
the node border foreground and selected styling instead of repainting gray cells.
Actual captures independently support improved border continuity in observed states.
Missing selected-state coverage must remain an evidence gap; it is not a claim
that an unobserved border is broken.

## Scope of conclusions

No renderer changes, new layout trials, installs, or new captures were made for
this audit. The fixed rubric and source expectations remain unchanged. The
all-eight-critique barrier still governs any skill proposal or stop decision.

## Concrete failures and blockers

### N01 — Border integrity fails; medium severity

Every one of the eleven visible node instances has two neutral RGB `(146,131,116)` border cells. The remaining outline uses the node's normal hue. All four corners and both sides are geometrically complete, so this is a **color continuity**, not missing geometry, failure.

The generator calls this cosmetic and its verification report still concludes that all mechanical checks pass. Neither statement changes the frozen requirement that **every** border cell, including handles and selected states, use consistent per-node color. Severity does not waive the failure.

### N02 — Conceptual color grouping fails; high severity

### N03 — Sparse animation fails; medium severity

- Views 02 and 03: `[34,20,1,2]`, `[34,28,1,2]`.

Each route has only three stem cells before its arrowhead; two are dots in these frames. That is visibly non-sparse on these short corridors. This finding does not introduce a numeric seven-cell threshold into the frozen rubric: the seven-cell separation statement is a **generator/skill claim contradicted by the capture**, while the rubric's actual requirement is sparse motion. No inference about backend particle implementation is necessary.

The dot glyphs stay off borders in all retained frames. They do not replace label text or arrowheads. All frames were audited, including selected-state text, and all seven source routes are covered. These positives do not cancel N03.

### N04 — Direction and slow-speed evidence is aliased; high-severity evidence gap

Frames are separated by approximately 2–3 seconds. Views 01/02 show lower-only → adjacent pair → upper-only → lower-only. ---
name: visualize
description: Build live ratatui node diagrams in Herdr panes. Preserve source relationships, make arrows and labels traceable, check actual text and ANSI output, and use a separate Astra worker for readability review. Report unsupported renderer features instead of hiding them. Use artifact for HTML documents and mermaid for diagrams inside chat.
---

# visualize

Build a JSON graph for `rataflow-view` and show it in a Herdr pane.
Use the mermaid tool for a diagram inside a chat reply. Use artifact for HTML.
Never paste terminal pane art or ANSI escapes into chat or an editor buffer.

## Establish the meaning before drawing

Read the relevant conversation or source. Later human corrections override
older generated diagrams. Old assistant claims are evidence, not verified facts.
Do not replay commands, inspect credentials, or contact hosts merely because
historical messages mention those actions.

Make a short coverage record before writing the spec:

- Required concepts, labels, addresses, roles, and location facts.
- Each relationship's endpoints, direction, actions, payloads, and qualifiers.
- Requested ordering, conceptual groups, and independent versus shared links.
- Animation requirements: which edges, direction, speed, and dot count.
- Uncertain facts and optional context. Keep uncertainty visible.

Do not reduce coverage to an edge count. A visible arrow can still lose meaning
when its label drops repair, verification, payload arguments, or an address prefix.
Shorten wording only when the displayed text retains the original meaning.
Use multiline node labels or a clearly identified note where useful. A glossary
in the generation report does not repair information missing from the diagram.

For software placement, distinguish runs-on/hosts from calls/reads/deploys.
For networks, distinguish physical connectivity from directional traffic.
State the arrow convention. Do not reverse a relationship to improve placement.

## Check capabilities before repeated layout work

Use the actual selected executable's schema and check output. Do not infer
support from an old skill, another installed binary, or a proposed feature.

The currently evaluated schema supports:

- `direction`: `tb` or `lr`.
- `theme`: `gruvbox`, `dark`, or `light`.
- `nodes`: objects with `id` and optional `label`.
- `edges`: objects with `from`, `to`, optional `label`, and optional `flow`.
- `layers`: arrays of node IDs; each node appears once. `""` reserves a slot.
- `flow`: a boolean or positive speed, not an independent dot count.

Unknown fields are rejected. An endpoint can create an implicit node.

These are current limits, not authoring mistakes:

- No declared bus/junction primitive provides one shared trunk and one split.
- No independent one-live-dot setting exists. Lower speed does not reduce count.
- Hue families follow geometric layers. There is no independent semantic-group
  or color-family field for concepts spread across different layers.
- Automatic labels can be missing or visually detached even after a clean check.

If a requirement needs an unsupported capability, name the missing capability
and stop that part. Do not substitute independent paths for an explicit bus,
disable required motion, invent fields, or claim that geometric colors encode
conceptual groups. A renderer change needs its own tested baseline.

## Preserve independent links and intentional branches

Independent redundant links must stay separate. Each needs an identifiable
source stem and target arrowhead. A crossing must not look like a connection.
Separate ports and zero shared cells do not prove that neighboring bends read well.

A source-requested shared medium or bus is different. Honor its explicit branch
semantics; never apply a universal separate-edge rule against that requirement.
The current renderer limitation must remain visible when it cannot draw that bus.

Keep the source-to-target route readable through every label and crossing.
A word on a route is acceptable only when its continuation and ownership remain
unambiguous. Reject text that masks the cue needed to choose between paths.
Identical labels do not excuse uncertain ownership.

## Choose layout and focused views

Choose conceptual groups before geometric layers. Keep related concepts near one
another. Check whether the actual layer hues support those concepts; do not claim
semantic grouping merely because nodes share a row or a color.

Measure the real pane. Natural zoom is 100%; do not shrink text to hide overflow.
Use `tb` when width is scarce and `lr` when height is scarce. Test extent rather
than treating an orientation rule as a guarantee. Rough budgets of 12 nodes and
16 edges are prompts to inspect density, not permission to delete information.

If one view is too dense, use focused views with repeated boundary nodes.
Map every required concept and relation to a visible view. Keep full source facts
and record intentional abstractions. Distinguish three coverage states:

1. Present in the spec.
2. Visually traceable from source to target.
3. Label meaning visibly and uniquely attached to that route.

Only the third is complete relationship coverage. Preserve meaningful location
and addressing annotations too. Do not replace distinct device branches with one
collapsed device box when the user requires the individual branches.

The control palette occupies the lower-left area. Keep boxes, routes, labels,
and notes clear of it. Verify complete corners and sides, not only node names.

## Bind checks and rendering to the same executable

Resolve one absolute executable path and one absolute spec path. In an eval,
use its frozen executable, never the globally installed version. Record the
executable and spec SHA-256 values with the exact executed commands.

Run the absolute executable with `--check` and save stdout, stderr, and exit code.
A successful exit validates the input; it does not approve readability.
Inspect every warning. Missing labels remain defects even when exit status is zero.

Inside Herdr, split a no-focus sibling at ratio 0.5. Use the current agent's tab,
not another session's pane. Use the Herdr CLI, never raw tmux.

```sh
# Open an even viewer pane without changing the focused agent pane
herdr pane split --current --direction right --ratio 0.5 --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Take the actual pane ID from the response. Launch the absolute executable and
absolute spec, then close that exact pane when the viewer exits:

```text
herdr pane run <pane-id> '<absolute-executable> <absolute-spec>; herdr pane close <pane-id>'
```

Quote real paths correctly. Do not rely on the parent command's PATH being
inherited by an already running pane shell. Bare `rataflow-view` is insufficient
when a particular frozen executable is required.

Measure rows/columns inside the viewer pane before launch. Preserve the measured
PTY dimensions separately from Herdr's chrome-inclusive rectangle. A command echo
is not proof that the viewer started: inspect the actual visible header.

Outside Herdr, explain the missing live surface and offer the mermaid tool.
Do not launch the interactive viewer inside the coding tool's non-TTY shell.

## Check actual output

Capture `herdr pane read <pane-id> --source visible` and the ANSI form using
`--format ansi`. Record actual capture times, state, and filenames. Text and ANSI
reads can occur in different animation phases; do not label them simultaneous.
Do not substitute filesystem modification time for a recorded capture event.

Check these independently:

- Every required concept and complete relationship meaning appears.
- Every arrow has a clear source stem, continuous path, and unique target head.
- Every label has one identifiable owning route, without consulting the JSON.
- Crossings, adjacent bends, and animation do not imply false continuations.
- Boxes, labels, routes, and notes fit without pan, zoom, or control occlusion.
- Every border side and corner is complete and uniformly colored.
- Related colors describe source concepts rather than arbitrary geometric depth.

For strict evaluation, capture each node occurrence selected as well as unselected.
A frame containing one selected node does not test every other node's selected
state. Determine selection from actual ANSI, not from an assumed Tab order.
Missing state evidence is blocked, not proof of a broken border or a full pass.

For required animation, record sufficiently close timestamped frames or a recording
to resolve movement on every requested route. Inspect short routes and bends.
Sparse snapshots of repeated dots can alias; changed hashes alone prove neither
direction nor slow speed. Preserve corners, arrowheads, labels, and border cells.
Optional motion may be omitted when it harms traceability. Required motion cannot
be removed to obtain a pass. Explicit one-dot requirements need renderer support.

## Independent review

After generation, use a separate `worker` on `openai/gpt-6-astra` as the judge.
During skill evaluations, generators use DeepSeek; Astra is reserved for judging.
Do not let the generator or renderer fixer approve its own result.

First give the judge only final raw captures, dimensions, and timestamps.
Require saved blind observations of inferred links, labels, groups, and defects.
Then reveal the relevant source, spec, checks, and coverage record to the same judge.
Require concrete edge names, capture coordinates, per-category verdicts, and a
clear distinction between observed failures and missing evidence.

A clean check, all labels present, or passing tests cannot replace this review.
If Astra or required evidence is unavailable, report blocked. Do not silently
substitute another model. Results arrive automatically; do not poll.
After a correction, ask for another review through `subagent_message` with new
captures. Never claim approval before the result arrives.

## Cleanup and final report

Keep an ownership record for every pane created, including rejected attempts.
Close only owned panes. Save exact cleanup commands and closure or final-layout
results. Do not invent missing execution history after review.

Report the spec paths, view coverage, reviewer verdict, and remaining defects.
State whether the result is approved, failed, or blocked. Separate skill-authoring
problems from renderer limits. Do not claim a renderer change as a skill-only gain.

Controls: drag nodes to move them, drag empty space to pan, scroll to zoom,
`f` to fit, and `q` or Esc to exit. Reopening restores the planned layout.
Dragging uses the existing fallback router; initial-layout guarantees do not
prove that every dragged arrangement remains readable.

# Skill proposal 02 — not evaluated or installed

This proposal follows all eight complete round01 critiques. It is not a new
round, a successful candidate, or evidence of an improved score. Final report
clarifications correct evidence coverage; they do not rerender any sample.

Parent skill SHA-256:
`9c5cea272a88300644cacda52c853c7c9169eeec91f0355d3460ee8741308d92`

The [proposed SKILL.md](SKILL.md) is separate from the working-tree skill and
the globally installed skill. Neither was replaced by this proposal.

## Finding-to-change map

| Change | Evidence from round01 |
|---|---|
| Inventory full meaning, qualifiers, roles, addresses, and uncertainty before layout | Homelab/server lose address and role context; Modal views lose action/payload meaning; GB300 confuses hosting with control protocols. |
| Distinguish spec presence, traced endpoints, and uniquely attached label meaning | Datacenter has 28 pairs in JSON but only 19 complete visual relationship passes; manager has missing and incomplete labels. |
| Reject label-covered routes and visually touching bends | Datacenter fabric paths cross text; homelab bends and moving dots create ambiguous continuations. |
| Preserve explicit physical-connectivity semantics and branch requirements | Datacenter backward arrows must retain source direction; GB300 must not substitute three independent routes for its requested trunk. |
| Check capabilities before retrying layouts | The schema lacks a bus primitive and independent one-dot control. Group hues still depend on geometric bands. |
| Bind every check and viewer launch to an absolute executable | Network commands use a bare name despite declaring a frozen BIN; its actual executed binary remains unproven. |
| Record exact commands, timestamps, PTY size, and cleanup for all attempts | Runtime has conflicting launch/time records; several cases omit rejected-attempt or probe cleanup evidence. |
| Capture each node occurrence selected; identify selection from ANSI | Seven cases lack complete selected-state proof. Several judges originally mistook view-level frames for every-node coverage; corrections are archived. Network also has an observed border-color failure. |
| Use time-resolved motion evidence and inspect every animated route | All three required-animation cases fail sparsity; coarse snapshots alias and cannot establish direction or speed. |
| Keep blind-first review and disclose failures rather than claiming a clean check means approval | All eight independent critiques reject the delivered output despite many successful check commands. |

## Limits this proposal cannot fix

Instructions cannot add a bus/junction declaration or independent live-dot count
to the frozen renderer. They also cannot add semantic-group color metadata or
make the label router reserve all required visual space. Those changes belong
in a separately tested renderer baseline, not an uncredited skill-only revision.

The color rule remains the frozen rule: related source concepts need related
hues and appropriate proximity. Global per-node color stability across views is
not a separate new gate. The proposal prevents misleading claims about what the
position-based palette represents; it does not silently amend the rubric.

## Why there is no rerun

The frozen stop rule permits stopping at an unsupported required capability.
GB300's explicit shared trunk and the manager's one-live-dot request reach that
boundary. Another skill-only full sweep cannot demonstrate those capabilities.
A rerun would consume eight new generators and eight judges without clearing
that known prerequisite. No improvement or two-revision convergence is claimed.

If renderer support is added, freeze the new binary and source as a new baseline.
Then test all eight cases with fresh DeepSeek generators and separate Astra judges.
Keep the same dataset, target size, and rubric. Preserve strict attempt limits;
round01 includes over-budget exploration and is not a clean bounded comparison.

DATACENTER-REDUNDANCY pass
Source-related pairs occupy related hue families. Fabric BL and rack leaves have aligned top edges at row 24 with related teal shades; both spines are above at row 12, racks below at row 34. BL1 extra row does not change tier. Cross-view hues are view-local, not stable global identity colors; the rubric does not require global identity colors and no unsupported global-color claim is credited.

GB300-RACK-SOFTWARE fail
The four-view topical separation helps, and v1 BMC/power endpoints have related pink shades. But color follows geometric depth rather than required residence groups: NVOS and its NMX software use different families; DCGM/driver/Fabric Manager use pink/green/blue, with no compute-host annotation. Repeated OOB identity changes family across views as depth changes. These are not documented source-defined residency tiers.
F07 Color encodes graph depth rather than the source residency groups: v3 separates NVOS (light teal #93c2b7) from hosted NMX-C/T (pink #d3869b), while grouping NVOS with NVSwitch BMC (teal #7daea3). In v4 DCGM is pink, Driver+CUDA green and Fabric Mgr blue with no compute-host grouping annotation. Source-defined related software residency is not represented by a related hue family or explicit grouping. Across views OOB LAN changes teal to amber when its geometric depth changes; this is not a declared semantic legend.

HOMELAB-NIC-TRACE fail
Virtual peers, bridges and the NIC pair are locally grouped, and path order is preserved. Related serial Verizon hops have unrelated hue families, while repeated concepts change hues across split views. Frozen layer-depth coloring does not preserve source concept groups (F6).
F6 View 3 gives the related Verizon aggregation and backbone hops unrelated green and blue hues merely because they occupy consecutive layout layers. The same host changes pink to teal across views and the same NIC pair changes pink to gold, with no semantic legend. Source ordering is retained, and local peer groupings work, but geometric depth is not a stable concept grouping across this split.

MODAL-MACHINE-MANAGER fail
Layout respects local chain order, but per-depth hues create unsupported mixed conceptual groups and inconsistent identities across views. Shared host/agent and gRPC concepts do not retain related hues while unrelated same-depth nodes are presented as one family. Source-defined concepts are not replaced by geometric rank merely because the renderer colors rank.
F08 Layer hues encode geometric depth rather than stable source concepts: v2 puts host agent with boot server and S3 while its host has another hue; v3 puts private gRPC with agent and public gRPC with queue/reconcile. Bare-metal machines changes from orange (v1) to gold (v2/v3) to pink (v4). No displayed legend/group explanation makes these source-backed conceptual categories; generation explicitly claims per-layer color grouping.

MODAL-RUNTIME fail
Geometric row depth determines hue, including unsupported same-hue groups of backend/filesystem/daemon and container/Blobnet. Source execution/container and filesystem/storage relations are not expressed as related hue families. The source does not define these geometric tiers; no visible legend qualifies them (F06). Cross-view color changes are corroboration, not a separate fixed-color requirement.
F06 The hue families encode geometric rows rather than the source-described execution/container and filesystem/storage concepts. Overview groups backend, filesystem and daemon as three green siblings while the closely related container and Blobnet form an unrelated shared blue tier; execution similarly gives backend/filesystem teal and container/Blobnet pink. No source-defined tier or legend supports those same-hue groups. Seams then pairs daemon with engine in pink. Cross-view hue changes corroborate the depth encoding, but hue stability alone is not an added rubric requirement.

NETWORK pass
Corrected on source-grouping consistency review; N02 is withdrawn. The related source roles WAN, Firewall, Core switch, Web tier, Redis/cache and DB tier remain near their connected neighbors in the three ordered chains. These are distinct named roles/tiers, each represented by one node in a view; the source does not define a multi-node same-tier hue group. Core-to-Web/Core-to-Redis and Web-to-Redis/Web-to-DB are distinct relations, not source-declared sibling color groups. Within each view the tier distinction and source order are clear. Cross-view Core/Web/DB hue drift is observed but does not itself assert a grouping or violate a global color identity requirement, which the frozen rubric does not contain. No source-backed misleading group is established; no legend or stable per-node cross-view hue is imposed as an added gate.

PIPELINE pass
The source-supported branch hierarchy is clear: CLI ingress, gateway, two sibling gateway destinations, queue-following worker, common persistence. Auth and queue share related pinks as sibling gateway destinations; queue/worker stay vertically near on the write branch, distinct from the Auth/read branch. No source-defined tier or order is reversed. This is not a claim that geometric depth proves common function. CLI shares selection gold, but the frozen category does not require exclusive accent allocation.

SERVER-NIC-LAYOUT fail
F3: Related server/NIC/Airtel concepts do not use related hue families; a gold layer mixes unlike source concepts. Repeated Arista changes color between views. Observed color encodes route depth rather than a source-backed conceptual grouping.
F3 Hue grouping follows geometric depth, not source concepts. Identical-model server1 and server2 use teal versus gold; inactive and active NIC concepts use gold versus pink. The top gold row combines inactive NICs, server2 and speculative spare addresses. The two Airtel stages use teal versus pink, while the repeated Arista gateway changes green in vA to gold in vB. No visible legend gives these source-backed conceptual color semantics.

# Round 01: stop at required renderer capabilities

**Result: 0/8 green cases. All eight cases fail. No candidate is approved.**

Eight fresh DeepSeek generators produced the samples. Eight separate Astra judges
saved blind observations, then compared the same evidence with the source.
All complete critiques arrived before the next skill proposal. The captain also
resolved selected-state overclaims and an unsupported global-color requirement.
Original reports remain archived; all eight blind records remain unchanged.

The fixed stop rule permits stopping at an unsupported required capability.
The frozen renderer cannot declare GB300's single shared trunk or independently
request one live dot per edge. More skill-only retries cannot add those controls.
This stop is not a claim that two skill revisions failed; none was evaluated.

## Final matrix

P = pass. F = fail. B = missing required evidence or capability. — = source-backed N/A.
A known failure still determines FAIL when another category is blocked.

| Case | Meaning | Arrows | Fit | Groups/color | Borders | Evidence | Animation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | P | P | P | P | B | B | F |
| Network | P | P | B | P | F | B | F |
| Homelab NIC trace | F | F | F | F | B | B | — |
| Server NIC layout | F | P | F | F | B | F | — |
| Datacenter redundancy | F | F | F | P | B | B | — |
| Modal machine manager | F | F | F | F | B | B | F |
| Modal runtime | F | P | P | F | B | F | — |
| GB300 rack software | F | F | F | F | B | B | — |

Of 51 applicable categories, **11 pass, 26 fail, and 14 are blocked**.
The recorded findings contain 12 critical, 33 high, and 7 medium entries.
These are reported findings, not a new weighted score or a unique-root-cause count.
The nominal comparison tuple is `(0, 11, -12, -33)`.

Round01 is the last and only completed baseline, so its last and best-observed
matrices are identical. It is not an eligible proof of improvement: execution
binding, state evidence, and attempt-budget problems remain. Cancelled round00
is excluded. There is no approved or successfully improved skill candidate.

Machine-readable results and report hashes: [matrix.json](matrix.json).
All complete critiques: [reviews/](reviews/).

## What failed

- **Pipeline:** all six relationships are readable. Adjacent simultaneous dots
  violate sparse motion. Four node occurrences lack their own selected evidence.
- **Network:** all seven relationships are readable. Actual captures show neutral
  border cells and adjacent dots. The launch used bare `rataflow-view`, so the
  record does not prove it executed the frozen binary. Do not attribute those
  border defects to the corrected renderer. Numeric zoom attestation is also
  blocked. Color passes after removing the unsupported global-stability rule.
- **Homelab:** 13 concepts and 14 relationships remain in JSON. Required address,
  role, and historical limitation details are missing. Six required relationship
  audits fail, plus four apparent-link audits. Touching or dot-masked bends and
  detached labels prevent clear reading.
- **Server:** eight arrows are traceable, but required address/AS context is lost.
  Colors mix unlike concepts. The recorded selected-node identity is also wrong
  for one capture; six node occurrences lack their own selected-state evidence.
- **Datacenter:** all 28 pairs remain in JSON. Only 19 complete relationship audits
  pass. Two paths cross label text, and seven other labels have uncertain owners.
  Source pair/tier grouping passes. Initial pane `w7E:p37` lacks raw closure proof;
  that is not proof of a leak.
- **Machine manager:** all 17 component IDs and 23 directed pairs remain in JSON,
  but repair, reprovision, verification, and boot-response arguments lose meaning.
  Two labels disappear. All eight selected animated routes violate the last
  one-live-dot correction. Full-pair presence does not establish full fidelity.
- **Runtime:** endpoint paths are traceable, but task-input/management and process
  meaning is incomplete. Groups do not match execution/storage concepts. Some
  launch, timestamp, and cleanup records conflict.
- **GB300:** three independent OOB paths replace the requested trunk. Hosting and
  protocol semantics are incomplete or incorrect, residence groups are unclear,
  and two labels have uncertain ownership. Some historical OOB→NVOS reachability
  remains unconfirmed; the renderer cannot resolve source uncertainty.

## Renderer boundary versus skill defects

The [frozen-source capability audit](capability-audit.md) identifies:

1. No bus/junction/shared-trunk declaration. The router allocates separate ports.
2. No independent live-dot count. `flow` controls speed; the periodic pattern can
   produce multiple dots and can replace ordinary bend glyphs.
3. No semantic-group color field independent of layout bands. This is a control
   limitation, not proof that every geometric layout must fail conceptual grouping.
4. Labels can obscure or detach from routes despite a clean check. This is an
   observed defect, not a proved impossibility for every alternate layout.

Meaning inventories, careful abbreviations, exact binary launches, complete
state captures, and honest cleanup records are skill/workflow changes. They do
not add renderer capabilities. The [proposed skill](../../proposals/02/SKILL.md)
addresses those authoring failures and stops honestly at unsupported features.
Its [change map](../../proposals/02/README.md) links the proposal to the critiques.
The proposal is **unevaluated and not installed**. The active working-tree skill
was not replaced after the round, and the global skill/binary were not updated.

Before another full evaluation, renderer support must demonstrate the explicit
trunk and independent one-dot requirement. Source-group color control and safe
label ownership also need work. Any renderer change requires a new frozen
baseline and all eight fresh DeepSeek samples with separate Astra judges.
The dataset, natural 77×47 target, and rubric must remain unchanged.

## Evidence corrections and execution limits

- Seven border categories are blocked because selected-state coverage is partial.
  No observed border defect is alleged in those seven cases. A frame with one
  selected node does not test the selected borders of all other visible nodes.
- Proven selected occurrences are 3/16 for homelab, 5/24 for datacenter, 4/27 for
  manager, 6/17 for runtime, and 4/19 for GB300. Superseded claims are archived.
- Network's color failure depended on an added global per-node hue-stability rule.
  Its judge withdrew that finding. The frozen related-concept hue rule remains.
  Other color failures identify source-backed grouping defects, not drift alone.
- Every source snapshot, expected/variant file, candidate, frozen binary, rubric,
  and frozen renderer-source hash still matches round metadata. The captain also
  checked all 522 final evidence records, schema fields, references, coordinates,
  animation applicability, worker role separation, and overall verdict logic.
- Hash verification proves file identity, not historical execution. Network's
  executable binding remains unproven despite its frozen binary hash matching.
- The generation limit was three local spec attempts per view. Datacenter records
  extra fabric alternatives beyond three and further merged/reference exploration.
  Network's attempt list has 13 entries, including duplicate/reference entries,
  and many alternatives without a clear bounded per-view accounting. These are
  protocol compliance problems, not evidence that the budget was satisfied.
  Final-view scoring does not excuse or hide that exploration.
- All generators reported cleanup. Some reports lack raw closure/probe evidence.
  Missing records remain blockers; current pane state cannot repair history.

## Regression checks

After review, without changing the renderer or frozen evidence:

- `cargo test --offline --manifest-path rataflow/Cargo.toml`: **46 tests pass**.
- `cargo clippy --offline --manifest-path rataflow/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **pass**.
- `uv run --offline scripts/test-rataflow.py`: **9/9 reported checks pass**;
  its opt-in cargo step is skipped, and cargo was run directly above.
- `git diff --check`: **pass**.

These checks do not overturn the failed visual evaluation. No new live sessions,
renderer changes, dependency additions, commits, installs, or remote access were
performed during final aggregation.

| Unevaluated proposal 02 | `bb2ccaeccca85ca52181d67fe7c0ceb785428d6179b2d6f9fa1dd294f15c265e` |

[metadata.json](metadata.json). Current orchestration state is [state.json](../../state.json).

# Language standard: near-ASD-STE100

Write all prose output at approximately 80% compliance with ASD-STE100
(Simplified Technical English). Apply these rules to all prose you write:

- Keep sentences short: one topic per sentence, target 15 words or fewer.
- Use the approved-verb principle: prefer simple, common verbs (make, show,
  start, use, check) over complex synonyms (utilize, facilitate, implement).
- Use the active voice.
- Prefer the present tense. Use the imperative form for instructions.
- Use one word or phrase per concept. Do not use synonyms for the same thing.
- Keep paragraphs to 6 sentences or fewer.

**Extension tool content is 100%, not 80%.** Every quiz, explain,
ask_user_question, and lesson call writes its question, options, details, and
prose at FULL compliance: short sentences, active voice, approved verbs, one
term per concept. No relaxations apply to these panels — the learner reads them
as the lesson itself.

Stay at 80%, not 100% for ordinary prose unless an active skill sets a stricter
standard. Apply the active skill before these relaxations. Otherwise, these
relaxations apply:

- Technical nouns, identifiers, and code stay as-is. Do not simplify names of
  files, APIs, tools, or errors.
- Complex sentences are allowed when a sentence would otherwise fragment into
  awkward chains (e.g. cause-and-effect or conditional statements).
- The 30-line answer cap, Markdown structure, and suggested follow-up questions
  come first. STE rules shape the prose inside that structure.
- Do not rewrite or refuse content that cannot fully comply (quotes, logs,
  poetry, human language in files). Apply the rules to your own prose only.

## Response shape

Write semantic Markdown only; Pi's theme owns presentation.

Keep final answers to 30 lines or less, and wrap prose near 100 characters per
line. The 30-line limit is a hard cap: if a complete answer would run longer,
fit the most important part into the cap and defer the rest to the suggested
follow-up questions at the end.

Prefer structure over walls of text:

- Use Markdown headings (`##`, `###`) for sections.
- Use bullet points for lists, enumerations, and multi-item findings.
- Lead with the direct answer or outcome; push context, caveats, and evidence
  below it.

End every response with a `## Suggested follow-up questions` section: 2–4
concrete, self-contained one-liners the user could send verbatim to continue the
thread. Use it for pieces that did not fit in the 30-line cap, or for natural
next decisions. Skip the section only for trivial acknowledgements (e.g. a bare
"Done.").

## Diagrams

When an answer presents a plan, a dependency structure, or a flow, call the
`mermaid` tool instead of writing a mermaid fence inline. Pass the diagram as
structured data: `type`, `direction`, `nodes` (id + label), `edges` (from,
to, optional label), plus `groups` for zones. Labels are copied verbatim —
never put double quotes in a label. The tool emits the source, validates it
locally (strict parse, exact structure match against your params, pane fit
on the chat's renderer), and returns in under a second. The validated
diagram is displayed to the user automatically as a transcript row; do not
write the fence in your reply. On `isError`, fix exactly what the error
names and call once more.

Keep diagrams small: about 7 nodes or fewer, short labels, prefer TD. The
pane is narrow; height is free. A diagram that needs scrolling carries too
many nodes — split the answer instead.

## Shell, python, and mcpScript call titles

Open every `bash` command, every `python` script, and every `mcpScript`
script with one comment line that states the intent of the call. The row
header shows it as the call title, next to the tool name.

```text
bash example:
# list files changed on this branch against main
git diff --name-only main...HEAD

python example:
# parse the session log for nested bash calls
rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(path)]

mcpScript example:
// fan out the workspace searches and filter failures
const settled = await Promise.allSettled(calls)
```

Rules:

- The comment is the first line, before any code.
- Start the comment with a verb. Use 10 to 15 words. State the intent, not
  the syntax.
- Do not end the comment with a period.
- Use one comment line. Do not write a comment block.
- A `#` comment after the first code line stays a normal comment, not a
  title.
- `mcpScript` scripts use a `//` comment, not `#`. The `// @options:`
  directive line comes after the title comment, never before it.
- A `//` comment after the first code line stays a normal comment, not a
  title.
- `powershell` calls take no title comment.

## Python tool preference

Run Python code with the `python` tool. Do not wrap Python in a `bash`
command.

- Do not use `python3 - <<` heredocs. Do not use `python3 -c` strings.
- Send the code as the `code` parameter. Send one snippet per call.
- A blocked `bash` call means: send the same code with the `python` tool.
- Run an existing script file (`python3 script.py`) in `bash` only when the
  script is the deliverable. Do not use it for inline data work.

## Edit tool paths

Send the edit tool's `path` relative to the session cwd, the same way
read calls do. Stored calls, result text, and downstream consumers then
carry the short, worktree-stable form.

- Send `path=src/main.rs`, not `path=/home/user/worktrees/fix-x/src/main.rs`.
- Keep the absolute form only when the file lies outside the session cwd.

## no-mistakes Herdr bridge invariants

The no-mistakes daemon's step agents run as visible Herdr subagent tabs when the triggering
session is inside Herdr (`scripts/install-nm-herdr-bridge`, upstream `agent_path_override.pi`).
These rules are load-bearing:

- Every step invocation owns a fresh tab and closes it after delivery; fixer rounds resume
  the durable session file in a fresh tab. Teardown (run terminal, session shutdown, extension
  reload) also closes panes so a later headless `--session` resume never meets a second writer;
  the shim then passthroughs to real pi with unchanged argv and stdin.
- Auto-exit subagents that finish cleanly close their whole Herdr tab (interactive subagents
  keep parking for the user), so an orphaned sibling pane can never hold the tab open after
  its session is done; the nvim-open extension likewise closes editor panes it created when
  a subagent session shuts down, while captain sessions leave editor panes open for the human.
- Subagent tab ownership is durable: the spawner's name registry (`subagent-registry.json`)
  marks each child `running` with its pane id until its result steer lands. A parent process
  death (deadline tab close, crash) leaves children ownerless — session_start adoption probes
  each still-marked pane: alive re-adopts it under a fresh watcher (result delivered, tab
  closed on real completion), dead finalizes it now (harvest, deliver, close the tab).
  `subagent_message` probes the same mark before resuming, so a live orphan is steered, never
  duplicated onto one session file.
- Pane state surfaces are Herdr's sanctioned ones only: `pane report-metadata --state-label`
  for display and the `herdr:blocked` event for the CI red state. Never report pane state
  from another source or impersonate a `herdr:` source - a second source cannot override the
  holder, and a seq-locked `herdr:` source mutes the managed reporter for the whole session.
- Step-agent tabs run `pi --no-extensions` with one closed set loaded explicitly
  (`STEP_AGENT_EXTENSIONS` in `pi/.pi/agent/extensions/no-mistakes-pane/bridge.ts`):
  pane-state reporters, capability tools (python, web-fetch, web-search, mermaid), and tab
  chrome. The parent's pipeline machinery (no-mistakes-gate, no-mistakes-pane,
  interactive-subagents, tuicr) and human-blocking tools never load inside a step agent -
  keep it that way when adding extensions. Every pi subagent spawned by interactive-subagents
  gets the parent's tool-call renderer as a baseline explicit `-e` (deduped by pi; skipped when
  absent) - the curated step-agent set above stays curated and unchanged.
- A run started from a Herdr captain session is owned by the `nm-orchestrator` subagent tab
  (tuicr-review architecture, `no-mistakes-pane/orchestrate.ts` + the bundled agent). It drives
  axi run/respond and owns the attach pane, gate panels, pane labels, and the step-agent
  bridge; the captain keeps read-only status/logs, abort as the escape hatch, and the
  orchestrator's final summary steer. Delegation never nests (subagent sessions execute
  directly) and falls back to direct driving without a TUI or spawn API - headless behavior
  is unchanged. The bundled nm-orchestrator declares `agent-dir: parent`, keeping the
  captain's configured agent dir instead of a repo-local `.pi/agent` redirect.
- Step-agent tab closes are clean exits: the tab's pi is asked to quit (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C
  fallback); after confirmed exit, `pane release-agent --source herdr:pi --agent pi` clears
  its identity before `pane close`. A terminated step agent must never surface as an
  agent-killed notification in the hosting session.

(`scripts/nm-test.sh`, `scripts/nm-lint.sh`) — the same offline suite as
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Gate/step agents must never improvise tests that launch live
sessions: no real pi sessions, no nvim, no tmux/multiplexer servers. The 2026-10-11
professor-test incident (run 01M4NRT2XKCHANREB6YFBPX6Q9) improvised a live harness,
timed out, and leaked nvim processes on the host.

Both runners discover targets with `git ls-files` — every `scripts/test-*` entry and
`pi/.pi/agent/extensions/**/*.test.mjs` joins automatically; never hand-list tests.
Per-component coverage, runtime SLA, and the full rules live in `docs/ci-tests/README.md`;
the no-mistakes runbook (commands, skip-vs-fail semantics, how to add coverage) is
`docs/ci-tests/no-mistakes-ci.md`. A new suite is a `scripts/test-<name>.*` entry with a
`# Paths:` header (`// Paths:` for .mjs) plus a `/simple` doc in `docs/ci-tests/`.

## CUDA LSP host invariant

NVIDIA ships no CUDA Toolkit for macOS Apple Silicon. `.cu` files get
local-symbol LSP only on the Mac (document symbols, local go-to-def/hover
work; CUDA-API symbols like `cudaMalloc`/`__nv_bfloat16` do not). Full
CUDA LSP needs the homelab/Linux CUDA Toolkit + a compile database.
`helpers/cuda_lsp.lua` detects this and notifies once per session; do not
try to stub CUDA headers or silence the clangd CUDA diagnostics. Authoritative
setup + homelab command: `docs/neovim-cuda-lsp.md`.

## Herdr pane tty sever and the stdin-reattach guard

Herdr (0.9.3; unfixed in 0.9.4/0.9.5) can reset a pane's tty to cooked mode
mid-session and let a Ctrl+D byte EOF the pane program's stdin — pi then
becomes an input-dead zombie (the "mermaid stuck input" incident; mermaid
itself is exonerated — see BUGS.md). `pi/.pi/agent/extensions/stdin-reattach.ts`
rescues the live session in place: it re-opens the pane tty path, restores
raw mode, feeds pi's own StdinBuffer, patches stdout/stderr onto the fresh
fds, re-negotiates terminal modes, and force-repaints. Keep that extension
loaded in every interactive session; it arms only when stdin is a real tty,
so rpc/json/print modes are unaffected, and it exits 129 only when no tty
can be re-opened at all (a real pane close). Note `node:fs` no longer exports
`execFileSync` on node 26 — take it from `node:child_process`.

# Language standard: near-ASD-STE100

Write all prose output at approximately 80% compliance with ASD-STE100
(Simplified Technical English). Apply these rules to all prose you write:

- Keep sentences short: one topic per sentence, target 15 words or fewer.
- Use the approved-verb principle: prefer simple, common verbs (make, show,
  start, use, check) over complex synonyms (utilize, facilitate, implement).
- Use the active voice.
- Prefer the present tense. Use the imperative form for instructions.
- Use one word or phrase per concept. Do not use synonyms for the same thing.
- Keep paragraphs to 6 sentences or fewer.

**Extension tool content is 100%, not 80%.** Every quiz, explain,
ask_user_question, and lesson call writes its question, options, details, and
prose at FULL compliance: short sentences, active voice, approved verbs, one
term per concept. No relaxations apply to these panels — the learner reads them
as the lesson itself.

Stay at 80%, not 100% for ordinary prose unless an active skill sets a stricter
standard. Apply the active skill before these relaxations. Otherwise, these
relaxations apply:

- Technical nouns, identifiers, and code stay as-is. Do not simplify names of
  files, APIs, tools, or errors.
- Complex sentences are allowed when a sentence would otherwise fragment into
  awkward chains (e.g. cause-and-effect or conditional statements).
- The 30-line answer cap, Markdown structure, and suggested follow-up questions
  come first. STE rules shape the prose inside that structure.
- Do not rewrite or refuse content that cannot fully comply (quotes, logs,
  poetry, human language in files). Apply the rules to your own prose only.

## Response shape

Write semantic Markdown only; Pi's theme owns presentation.

Keep final answers to 30 lines or less, and wrap prose near 100 characters per
line. The 30-line limit is a hard cap: if a complete answer would run longer,
fit the most important part into the cap and defer the rest to the suggested
follow-up questions at the end.

Prefer structure over walls of text:

- Use Markdown headings (`##`, `###`) for sections.
- Use bullet points for lists, enumerations, and multi-item findings.
- Lead with the direct answer or outcome; push context, caveats, and evidence
  below it.

End every response with a `## Suggested follow-up questions` section: 2–4
concrete, self-contained one-liners the user could send verbatim to continue the
thread. Use it for pieces that did not fit in the 30-line cap, or for natural
next decisions. Skip the section only for trivial acknowledgements (e.g. a bare
"Done.").

## Diagrams

When an answer presents a plan, a dependency structure, or a flow, call the
`mermaid` tool instead of writing a mermaid fence inline. Pass the diagram as
structured data: `type`, `direction`, `nodes` (id + label), `edges` (from,
to, optional label), plus `groups` for zones. Labels are copied verbatim —
never put double quotes in a label. The tool emits the source, validates it
locally (strict parse, exact structure match against your params, pane fit
on the chat's renderer), and returns in under a second. The validated
diagram is displayed to the user automatically as a transcript row; do not
write the fence in your reply. On `isError`, fix exactly what the error
names and call once more.

Keep diagrams small: about 7 nodes or fewer, short labels, prefer TD. The
pane is narrow; height is free. A diagram that needs scrolling carries too
many nodes — split the answer instead.

## Shell, python, and mcpScript call titles

Open every `bash` command, every `python` script, and every `mcpScript`
script with one comment line that states the intent of the call. The row
header shows it as the call title, next to the tool name.

```text
bash example:
# list files changed on this branch against main
git diff --name-only main...HEAD

python example:
# parse the session log for nested bash calls
rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(path)]

mcpScript example:
// fan out the workspace searches and filter failures
const settled = await Promise.allSettled(calls)
```

Rules:

- The comment is the first line, before any code.
- Start the comment with a verb. Use 10 to 15 words. State the intent, not
  the syntax.
- Do not end the comment with a period.
- Use one comment line. Do not write a comment block.
- A `#` comment after the first code line stays a normal comment, not a
  title.
- `mcpScript` scripts use a `//` comment, not `#`. The `// @options:`
  directive line comes after the title comment, never before it.
- A `//` comment after the first code line stays a normal comment, not a
  title.
- `powershell` calls take no title comment.

## Python tool preference

Run Python code with the `python` tool. Do not wrap Python in a `bash`
command.

- Do not use `python3 - <<` heredocs. Do not use `python3 -c` strings.
- Send the code as the `code` parameter. Send one snippet per call.
- A blocked `bash` call means: send the same code with the `python` tool.
- Run an existing script file (`python3 script.py`) in `bash` only when the
  script is the deliverable. Do not use it for inline data work.

## Edit tool paths

Send the edit tool's `path` relative to the session cwd, the same way
read calls do. Stored calls, result text, and downstream consumers then
carry the short, worktree-stable form.

- Send `path=src/main.rs`, not `path=/home/user/worktrees/fix-x/src/main.rs`.
- Keep the absolute form only when the file lies outside the session cwd.

## Python packaging

## Sidekick and Herdr session invariants

Treat repository, worktree, and session identity as three distinct concepts:

- For Herdr server replacement from Codex, follow the
  [color-safe live handoff procedure](README.md#herdr-server-handoff).
- A Git repository owns exactly one Herdr Workspace. Resolve repository identity from Git's shared common directory,
  so the primary checkout and every linked worktree reuse that same Herdr Workspace.
- A non-`main` Git worktree owns at most one durable Sidekick session. The session runs with that worktree as its cwd,
  inside the repository's Herdr Workspace. The `main` checkout may own multiple named durable sessions.
- If a user asks to launch a session in a non-`main` worktree that already owns one, focus and reuse the existing
  session. On `main`, reuse only an exact session-name match.
- If a user needs another durable session from a non-`main` worktree, create or select a different worktree first.
  Short-lived subagents may run beneath the owning session, but they do not become additional durable Sidekick picker
  sessions for that worktree.
- Do not create one Herdr Workspace per worktree, branch, feature, task, backend, or session label.
- Keep internal Herdr agent names available for routing and lifecycle operations, but do not use them as the primary
  picker identity.

## Worktree tool for change work

Agents making repo changes do not work from `main`. `pi/.pi/agent/extensions/worktree.ts` registers the `worktree`
tool: it creates or reuses `~/.herdr/worktrees/<repo>/<type>-<slug>` from local `main` (always `--no-focus`) and
launches an auto-exit `worker` subagent in the worktree session's first tab, via `executeSubagent` with an internal
`pane` override (guarded against the parent pane, agent-hosting panes, and cwd mismatches). The worker's result
steers back automatically; on clean completion its tab closes and the picker row folds until `herdr worktree open`.
Branches are ownership-marked (`branch.<b>.piWorktree` in git config, the gh-dash-open-pr pattern); anything the tool
does not own is refused. Teardown after ship stays with `/cleanup`.

Extension tools captains rarely call register with `exposure: "deferred"`: `quiz`, `explain`,
`problem`, `conclude`, `lesson`, `run-command`, `nvim_open`, `tuicr`, `tuicr_review`, `tuicr_reply`,
`no_mistakes_axi`.
Deferred tools stay out of the captain's system prompt, tool list, and rules. Subagent profiles
activate what they need through their `tools:` allowlist — professor, tuicr-review, and
nm-orchestrator already name these. Captains reach the rest through `tool_search`, enabled via
`defaultTools` in `settings.json` (which also pins `+worktree`). Register new rarely-used tools
deferred and name them in the profiles that need them. The MCP namespace proxies
(`mcp__browserbase`, `mcp__oreilly`, `mcp__mcp`) stay direct: the adapter re-activates them and
`mcp:<server>` references in tool-groups and slow-mode rely on them.

Reason: terminal-browser panes died with `pixel engine: unexpected end of file`

artifacts under herdr on both 0.9.3+patch and 0.9.5+patch, plus higher CPU;
keep `render.presenter=auto` until upstream PRs #157/#191 land. After any

## no-mistakes Herdr bridge invariants

The no-mistakes daemon's step agents run as visible Herdr subagent tabs when the triggering
session is inside Herdr (`scripts/install-nm-herdr-bridge`, upstream `agent_path_override.pi`).
These rules are load-bearing:

- Every step invocation owns a fresh tab and closes it after delivery; fixer rounds resume
  the durable session file in a fresh tab. Teardown (run terminal, session shutdown, extension
  reload) also closes panes so a later headless `--session` resume never meets a second writer;
  the shim then passthroughs to real pi with unchanged argv and stdin.
- Auto-exit subagents that finish cleanly close their whole Herdr tab (interactive subagents
  keep parking for the user), so an orphaned sibling pane can never hold the tab open after
  its session is done; the nvim-open extension likewise closes editor panes it created when
  a subagent session shuts down, while captain sessions leave editor panes open for the human.
- Subagent tab ownership is durable: the spawner's name registry (`subagent-registry.json`)
  marks each child `running` with its pane id until its result steer lands. A parent process
  death (deadline tab close, crash) leaves children ownerless — session_start adoption probes
  each still-marked pane: alive re-adopts it under a fresh watcher (result delivered, tab
  closed on real completion), dead finalizes it now (harvest, deliver, close the tab).
  `subagent_message` probes the same mark before resuming, so a live orphan is steered, never
  duplicated onto one session file.
- Pane state surfaces are Herdr's sanctioned ones only: `pane report-metadata --state-label`
  for display and the `herdr:blocked` event for the CI red state. Never report pane state
  from another source or impersonate a `herdr:` source - a second source cannot override the
  holder, and a seq-locked `herdr:` source mutes the managed reporter for the whole session.
- Step-agent tabs run `pi --no-extensions` with one closed set loaded explicitly
  (`STEP_AGENT_EXTENSIONS` in `pi/.pi/agent/extensions/no-mistakes-pane/bridge.ts`):
  pane-state reporters, capability tools (python, web-fetch, web-search, mermaid), and tab
  chrome. The parent's pipeline machinery (no-mistakes-gate, no-mistakes-pane,
  interactive-subagents, tuicr) and human-blocking tools never load inside a step agent -
  keep it that way when adding extensions. Every pi subagent spawned by interactive-subagents
  gets the parent's tool-call renderer as a baseline explicit `-e` (deduped by pi; skipped when
  absent) - the curated step-agent set above stays curated and unchanged.
- A run started from a Herdr captain session is owned by the `nm-orchestrator` subagent tab
  (tuicr-review architecture, `no-mistakes-pane/orchestrate.ts` + the bundled agent). It drives
  axi run/respond and owns the attach pane, gate panels, pane labels, and the step-agent
  bridge; the captain keeps read-only status/logs, abort as the escape hatch, and the
  orchestrator's final summary steer. Delegation never nests (subagent sessions execute
  directly) and falls back to direct driving without a TUI or spawn API - headless behavior
  is unchanged. The bundled nm-orchestrator declares `agent-dir: parent`, keeping the
  captain's configured agent dir instead of a repo-local `.pi/agent` redirect.
- Step-agent tab closes are clean exits: the tab's pi is asked to quit (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C
  fallback); after confirmed exit, `pane release-agent --source herdr:pi --agent pi` clears
  its identity before `pane close`. A terminated step agent must never surface as an
  agent-killed notification in the hosting session.

## no-mistakes gate test and lint runners

The gate's Test and Lint steps run the pinned offline runners from `.no-mistakes.yaml`
(`scripts/nm-test.sh`, `scripts/nm-lint.sh`) — the same offline suite as
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Gate/step agents must never improvise tests that launch live
sessions: no real pi sessions, no nvim, no tmux/multiplexer servers. The 2026-10-11
professor-test incident (run 01M4NRT2XKCHANREB6YFBPX6Q9) improvised a live harness,
timed out, and leaked nvim processes on the host.

Both runners discover targets with `git ls-files` — every `scripts/test-*` entry and
`pi/.pi/agent/extensions/**/*.test.mjs` joins automatically; never hand-list tests.
Per-component coverage, runtime SLA, and the full rules live in `docs/ci-tests/README.md`;
the no-mistakes runbook (commands, skip-vs-fail semantics, how to add coverage) is
`docs/ci-tests/no-mistakes-ci.md`. A new suite is a `scripts/test-<name>.*` entry with a
`# Paths:` header (`// Paths:` for .mjs) plus a `/simple` doc in `docs/ci-tests/`.

## CUDA LSP host invariant

NVIDIA ships no CUDA Toolkit for macOS Apple Silicon. `.cu` files get
local-symbol LSP only on the Mac (document symbols, local go-to-def/hover
work; CUDA-API symbols like `cudaMalloc`/`__nv_bfloat16` do not). Full
CUDA LSP needs the homelab/Linux CUDA Toolkit + a compile database.
`helpers/cuda_lsp.lua` detects this and notifies once per session; do not
try to stub CUDA headers or silence the clangd CUDA diagnostics. Authoritative
setup + homelab command: `docs/neovim-cuda-lsp.md`.

## Herdr pane tty sever and the stdin-reattach guard

Herdr (0.9.3; unfixed in 0.9.4/0.9.5) can reset a pane's tty to cooked mode
mid-session and let a Ctrl+D byte EOF the pane program's stdin — pi then
becomes an input-dead zombie (the "mermaid stuck input" incident; mermaid
itself is exonerated — see BUGS.md). `pi/.pi/agent/extensions/stdin-reattach.ts`
rescues the live session in place: it re-opens the pane tty path, restores
raw mode, feeds pi's own StdinBuffer, patches stdout/stderr onto the fresh
fds, re-negotiates terminal modes, and force-repaints. Keep that extension
loaded in every interactive session; it arms only when stdin is a real tty,
so rpc/json/print modes are unaffected, and it exits 129 only when no tty
can be re-opened at all (a real pane close). Note `node:fs` no longer exports
`execFileSync` on node 26 — take it from `node:child_process`.

## What landed in pass 1

- **Renderer rework** (`rataflow/src/router.rs` new, `flow_edge.rs`, `lib.rs`, `main.rs`): per-side ports, reserved stems, A* corridors, `⌒` bridges instead of false tees, layer-family colors, inherited node border styles, fixed 100% zoom with `--check` fit/readability warnings. 46 Rust tests + clean Clippy, offline Python suite green.

- **Result: 0/8 green.** 11 pass / 26 fail / 14 blocked of 51 categories; 12 critical, 33 high findings.
- **Stop reason:** required capabilities do not exist — explicit shared trunk (GB300), one-live-dot animation control, semantic-group color, safe label ownership. Proposal 02 written but **unevaluated and not installed**.

| Research + usage scout | 2 | 46 | $0.23 |

text:
# Round 01: stop at required renderer capabilities

**Result: 0/8 green cases. All eight cases fail. No candidate is approved.**

Eight fresh DeepSeek generators produced the samples. Eight separate Astra judges
saved blind observations, then compared the same evidence with the source.
All complete critiques arrived before the next skill proposal. The captain also
resolved selected-state overclaims and an unsupported global-color requirement.
Original reports remain archived; all eight blind records remain unchanged.

The fixed stop rule permits stopping at an unsupported required capability.
The frozen renderer cannot declare GB300's single shared trunk or independently
request one live dot per edge. More skill-only retries cannot add those controls.
This stop is not a claim that two skill revisions failed; none was evaluated.

## Final matrix

P = pass. F = fail. B = missing required evidence or capability. — = source-backed N/A.
A known failure still determines FAIL when another category is blocked.

| Case | Meaning | Arrows | Fit | Groups/color | Borders | Evidence | Animation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | P | P | P | P | B | B | F |
| Network | P | P | B | P | F | B | F |
| Homelab NIC trace | F | F | F | F | B | B | — |
| Server NIC layout | F | P | F | F | B | F | — |
| Datacenter redundancy | F | F | F | P | B | B | — |
| Modal machine manager | F | F | F | F | B | B | F |
| Modal runtime | F | P | P | F | B | F | — |
| GB300 rack software | F | F | F | F | B | B | — |

Of 51 applicable categories, **11 pass, 26 fail, and 14 are blocked**.
The recorded findings contain 12 critical, 33 high, and 7 medium entries.
These are reported findings, not a new weighted score or a unique-root-cause count.
The nominal comparison tuple is `(0, 11, -12, -33)`.

Round01 is the last and only completed baseline, so its last and best-observed
matrices are identical. It is not an eligible proof of improvement: execution
binding, state evidence, and attempt-budget problems remain. Cancelled round00
is excluded. There is no approved or successfully improved skill candidate.

Machine-readable results and report hashes: [matrix.json](matrix.json).
All complete critiques: [reviews/](reviews/).

## What failed

- **Pipeline:** all six relationships are readable. Adjacent simultaneous dots
  violate sparse motion. Four node occurrences lack their own selected evidence.
- **Network:** all seven relationships are readable. Actual captures show neutral
  border cells and adjacent dots. The launch used bare `rataflow-view`, so the
  record does not prove it executed the frozen binary. Do not attribute those
  border defects to the corrected renderer. Numeric zoom attestation is also
  blocked. Color passes after removing the unsupported global-stability rule.
- **Homelab:** 13 concepts and 14 relationships remain in JSON. Required address,
  role, and historical limitation details are missing. Six required relationship
  audits fail, plus four apparent-link audits. Touching or dot-masked bends and
  detached labels prevent clear reading.
- **Server:** eight arrows are traceable, but required address/AS context is lost.
  Colors mix unlike concepts. The recorded selected-node identity is also wrong
  for one capture; six node occurrences lack their own selected-state evidence.
- **Datacenter:** all 28 pairs remain in JSON. Only 19 complete relationship audits
  pass. Two paths cross label text, and seven other labels have uncertain owners.
  Source pair/tier grouping passes. Initial pane `w7E:p37` lacks raw closure proof;
  that is not proof of a leak.
- **Machine manager:** all 17 component IDs and 23 directed pairs remain in JSON,
  but repair, reprovision, verification, and boot-response arguments lose meaning.
  Two labels disappear. All eight selected animated routes violate the last
  one-live-dot correction. Full-pair presence does not establish full fidelity.
- **Runtime:** endpoint paths are traceable, but task-input/management and process
  meaning is incomplete. Groups do not match execution/storage concepts. Some
  launch, timestamp, and cleanup records conflict.
- **GB300:** three independent OOB paths replace the requested trunk. Hosting and
  protocol semantics are incomplete or incorrect, residence groups are unclear,
  and two labels have uncertain ownership. Some historical OOB→NVOS reachability
  remains unconfirmed; the renderer cannot resolve source uncertainty.

## Renderer boundary versus skill defects

The [frozen-source capability audit](capability-audit.md) identifies:

1. No bus/junction/shared-trunk declaration. The router allocates separate ports.
2. No independent live-dot count. `flow` controls speed; the periodic pattern can
   produce multiple dots and can replace ordinary bend glyphs.
3. No semantic-group color field independent of layout bands. This is a control
   limitation, not proof that every geometric layout must fail conceptual grouping.
4. Labels can obscure or detach from routes despite a clean check. This is an
   observed defect, not a proved impossibility for every alternate layout.

Meaning inventories, careful abbreviations, exact binary launches, complete
state captures, and honest cleanup records are skill/workflow changes. They do
not add renderer capabilities. The [proposed skill](../../proposals/02/SKILL.md)
addresses those authoring failures and stops honestly at unsupported features.

## What the round taught

- **Meaning was lost before drawing.** 5 of 8 cases fail semantic fidelity: addresses, roles, action arguments, uncertainty. Compaction dropped them, so better routing never got a chance to help.
- **Presence is not fidelity.** Datacenter kept all 28 pairs and manager kept 23, yet only 19 datacenter relations read traceably. A complete JSON proves nothing about a reader.
- **Labels became the second routing problem.** Text covered routes in datacenter, seven label owners were ambiguous, and two manager labels vanished.
- **Fit is a composition choice.** Two to four views is right at 77×47, but each split needs a source-to-view coverage map or meaning leaks at the seam.
- **Color belongs to the renderer, not the layout.** Band-derived hues express geometry, not concepts; four cases fail grouping for that reason.
- **Unproven is not pass.** 14 blocked categories were missing selected-state, cleanup, or binary-binding evidence. Meanwhile 8/8 judges rejected samples whose own `--check` was clean.

## Skill changes

- **Meaning ledger first:** list source facts, then mark each drawn, abbreviated, or dropped with a reason. No silent loss.
- **Relation audit per edge:** direction, both endpoints, label owner, traced path, and the view that carries it.
- **Capability preflight:** read the renderer feature list and stop when a required semantic (single trunk, one dot) has no primitive.
- **Evidence recipe:** absolute binary path and hash, measured PTY size, zoom, one selected capture per node occurrence, time-sampled animation, cleanup probe.

## Renderer changes (rataflow)

- **`trunk` declaration** with branch points, so a real bus is not three coincident lines.
- **Per-edge dot policy:** count, cadence, and a rule that dots never replace bend glyphs.
- **Semantic `group` field** mapping to palette families, replacing flow-axis bands.
- **Label cells reserved as obstacles**, plus diagnostics for text-covered routes and ambiguous label owners.

## Harness changes

- Enforce 4 views / 3 attempts with counters instead of honor-system logs.
- One capture script that emits text, ANSI, selected frames, hashes, a coverage table, and a binary stamp.
- Sol judge packet builder, and a round-02 rubric copy with only `required_reviewer_model` changed.

## Suggested follow-up questions

- Which renderer change should land first if only one can: trunk, dots, group color, or label reservation?
- Show the skill's new meaning-ledger and relation-audit templates as concrete examples.
- Write the round-02 acceptance gates before any code changes.
