old2 = (
    "        if let Some(description) = section.description.as_deref() {\n"
    "            put_world_text(\n"
    "                frame,\n"
    "                flow,\n"
    "                canvas,\n"
    "                section.header.0,\n"
    "                section.header.1 + 1,\n"
    "                description,\n"
    "                background.fg(palette.subtle),\n"
    "            );\n"
    "        }\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}"
)

DOT = "\u00b7"
TL, TR, BL, BR = "\u2554", "\u2557", "\u255a", "\u255d"
HZ, VT = "\u2550", "\u2551"

new2 = (
    "        if let Some(description) = section.description.as_deref() {\n"
    "            put_world_text(\n"
    "                frame,\n"
    "                flow,\n"
    "                canvas,\n"
    "                section.header.0,\n"
    "                section.header.1 + 1,\n"
    "                description,\n"
    "                background.fg(palette.subtle),\n"
    "            );\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        if let Some((fx, fy, fw, fh)) = section.frame {\n"
    "            draw_dotted_frame(frame, flow, canvas, fx, fy, fw, fh, palette.subtle);\n"
    "        }\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    draw_double_borders(frame, flow, canvas, sections, palette.text);\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "/// Paints a dotted rectangle: the boundary of a zoomed-in component's\n"
    "/// contents. Dots never read as a node border, so the frame says \"inside\n"
    "/// this box\" instead of looking like another element.\n"
    "#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n"
    "fn draw_dotted_frame(\n"
    "    frame: &mut Frame,\n"
    "    flow: &Graph,\n"
    "    canvas: Rect,\n"
    "    x: i32,\n"
    "    y: i32,\n"
    "    w: i32,\n"
    "    h: i32,\n"
    "    color: Color,\n"
    ") {\n"
    "    let style = Style::default().bg(flow.theme.palette().canvas_bg).fg(color);\n"
    "    if w < 2 || h < 2 {\n"
    "        return;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    let mut line = String::new();\n"
    "    for _ in 0..w {\n"
    f"        line.push('{DOT}');\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for row in [y, y + h - 1] {\n"
    "        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x, row, &line, style);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for row in (y + 1)..(y + h - 1) {\n"
    f"        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x, row, \"{DOT}\", style);\n"
    f"        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x + w - 1, row, \"{DOT}\", style);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "/// Repaints a zoom parent's border with double-line glyphs: the box a\n"
    "/// reader can zoom into wears a second ring.\n"
    "fn draw_double_borders(\n"
    "    frame: &mut Frame,\n"
    "    flow: &Graph,\n"
    "    canvas: Rect,\n"
    "    sections: &[SectionReport],\n"
    "    color: Color,\n"
    ") {\n"
    "    let focus: Vec<&str> = sections\n"
    "        .iter()\n"
    "        .flat_map(|section| section.focus.iter().map(String::as_str))\n"
    "        .collect();\n"
    "    if focus.is_empty() {\n"
    "        return;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    let style = Style::default().bg(flow.theme.palette().canvas_bg).fg(color);\n"
    "    for node in flow.nodes() {\n"
    "        if !focus.contains(&node.id.as_str()) {\n"
    "            continue;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        let x0 = node.position.x as i32;\n"
    "        let y0 = node.position.y as i32;\n"
    "        let w = node.width as i32;\n"
    "        let h = node.height as i32;\n"
    "        if w < 2 || h < 2 {\n"
    "            continue;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        let x1 = x0 + w - 1;\n"
    "        let y1 = y0 + h - 1;\n"
    f"        for (glyph, cx, cy) in [('{TL}', x0, y0), ('{TR}', x1, y0), ('{BL}', x0, y1), ('{BR}', x1, y1)] {{\n"
    "            put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, cx, cy, &glyph.to_string(), style);\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        let mut across = String::new();\n"
    "        for _ in 1..w - 1 {\n"
    f"            across.push('{HZ}');\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        for row in [y0, y1] {\n"
    "            put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x0 + 1, row, &across, style);\n"
    "        }\n"
    "        for row in (y0 + 1)..y1 {\n"
    f"            put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x0, row, \"{VT}\", style);\n"
    f"            put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x1, row, \"{VT}\", style);\n"
    "        }\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}"
)
assert t.count(old2) == 1, "heading block not found"
t = t.replace(old2, new2)
p.write_text(t)
print("drawing added")

    parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=47)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.select_all:
        app_argv.append("--select-all")
    app_argv.append(args.spec)
    status, data = run(args.bin, app_argv, args.cols, args.rows)
    # A pty hands back CRLF; the dump is a plain-text file and the recorded
    # `viewport:` line has to match the validator's anchored pattern exactly.
    text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").replace("\r\n", "\n")
    text = text.replace("\r", "").replace("\x1b", "")

            "the pty size did not reach the app",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    return 0 if status == 0 else status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

from pathlib import Path

p = Path("rataflow/src/lib.rs")
t = p.read_text()

DOT = "\u00b7"

old = (
    "    let mut line = String::new();\n"
    "    for _ in 0..w {\n"
    f"        line.push('{DOT}');\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for row in [y, y + h - 1] {\n"
    "        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x, row, &line, style);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for row in (y + 1)..(y + h - 1) {\n"
    f"        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x, row, \"{DOT}\", style);\n"
    f"        put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x + w - 1, row, \"{DOT}\", style);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}"
)

new = (
    "    let mut cells: Vec<(i32, i32)> = Vec::new();\n"
    "    for cx in x..(x + w) {\n"
    "        cells.push((cx, y));\n"
    "        cells.push((cx, y + h - 1));\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for cy in (y + 1)..(y + h - 1) {\n"
    "        cells.push((x, cy));\n"
    "        cells.push((x + w - 1, cy));\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    for (cx, cy) in cells {\n"
    f"        put_world_text_if_blank(frame, flow, canvas, cx, cy, '{DOT}', style);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "/// Writes one glyph at a world cell ONLY while that cell is blank: the\n"
    "/// dotted boundary is scenery, so a node border, a relation label, or a dot\n"
    "/// always wins over it. Painting over them erased text or hid crossing dots.\n"
    "fn put_world_text_if_blank(\n"
    "    frame: &mut Frame,\n"
    "    flow: &Graph,\n"
    "    canvas: Rect,\n"
    "    x: i32,\n"
    "    y: i32,\n"
    "    glyph: char,\n"
    "    style: Style,\n"
    ") {\n"
    "    let viewport = flow.viewport();\n"
    "    let (px, py) = viewport.world_to_screen(Position::new(x as f64, y as f64));\n"
    "    let tx = canvas.x as i64 + px.round() as i64;\n"
    "    let ty = canvas.y as i64 + py.round() as i64;\n"
    "    if tx < canvas.x as i64\n"
    "        || ty < canvas.y as i64\n"
    "        || tx >= (canvas.x + canvas.width) as i64\n"
    "        || ty >= (canvas.y + canvas.height) as i64\n"
    "    {\n"
    "        return;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    if frame.buffer_mut()[(tx as u16, ty as u16)].symbol() != \" \" {\n"
    "        return;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    put_world_text(frame, flow, canvas, x, y, &glyph.to_string(), style);\n"
    "}"
)

assert t.count(old) == 1, "dotted frame body not found"
t = t.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(t)
print("blank-only painting applied")

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
p = Path("docs/visualize-eval/proposals/13/SKILL.md")
t = p.read_text()
import re
start = t.index("- **The expanded contents sit in a dotted box:**")
end = t.index("- **Keep one reading direction across the canvas.**")
new = """- **The zoom parent's box GROWS to contain what it expands.** Name the
  nested cells in a `containers` entry on the diagram that holds them:
  `"containers": [{"label": "Machine manager", "members": ["api", "q",
  "rec", "db"]}]`. The box is drawn as a real double-bordered rectangle
  around those nodes, with its label set into the top edge, and the
  members render inside it. Containment is then literal: a reader sees
  the contents sitting in the box instead of inferring it from a tag.
- **Keep the members contiguous.** A container is a rectangle, so it
  encloses everything inside its bounding box: put the nested cells in
  one band (a rank or a short chain), or the box will swallow the
  external actors that happen to sit between them. If a service must be
  separated from the rest, give it its own container entry - several
  boxes are allowed.
- **Relations cross the boundary, they never run along it.** An edge
  leaving or entering the box keeps its own cells, so the border shows a
  gap where the relation passes: that reads as a connection, not as a
  break.

# visualize

Live visualizations rendered by ratatui, in a real terminal pane — the
surface the chat transcript cannot host, because it cannot run a TUI.
Today this skill renders node graphs: the `rataflow-view` binary (crate at
`rataflow/` in the dotfiles repo, built on the rataflow library) turns a
JSON spec into a pane the human can drag, pan, and zoom. Lay the graph out
so it fits on a single screen: in fullscreen the pane sits beside the chat
text, and the whole graph must read without pan or zoom. Edges render as
arrows; an optional `flow` field adds slow dots that travel source →
target.

## Routing: pick the surface first

This skill owns the ratatui surfaces — live, terminal-native rendering.
The vendored `artifact` skill routes graph-shaped requests here by
default. The full surface map:

| Destination | Use |
|---|---|
| pi chat reply | `mermaid` tool (grok-mermaid) |
| Static ANSI in shell output or a file | mermaid skill → mmdflux |
| PNG image | mermaid skill → mermaid.ink |
| Live interactive node graph in a pane | this skill → rataflow-view |
| HTML page (deck, dashboard, infographic) | artifact skill → terminal-browser pane |

Never paste rataflow pane art or ANSI escapes into pi chat or nvim buffers.

Use rataflow-view when the human should *explore* the graph: many nodes,
rearranging, tracing edges, zooming into one region. Use mermaid when the diagram is
part of an answer (chat, doc, PR).

## Read the relationships first

This skill is not a network-diagram tool; it draws *relationships*. Before
writing the spec, say what each relationship is — one sentence per edge
group is enough:

- **Direction.** Every edge points somewhere. `from` is the producer,
  sender, or caller; `to` is the consumer, receiver, or callee. If the
  relationship is bidirectional in reality, draw two edges or pick the
  dominant direction and say so in the label.
- **Names.** Label edges with the relationship, not the endpoints: verbs
  or link tech ("enqueue", "grpc", "10 GbE", "replicates"). Label nodes
  with what they *are*, a few words at most.

Layout direction: `tb` for pipelines and hierarchies (stages read top to
bottom), `lr` for request flow that reads left to right. Pick the one that
matches how the human describes the flow ("client → … → db" is `lr`).

## Spec format

Write a JSON file. Nodes are optional — every edge endpoint becomes a
node, and `label` defaults to `id`:

## The blocking gap
The installed skill — `agents/.agents/skills/visualize/SKILL.md`, what `/visualize` actually reads — has **no mention of `containers`, C4, or the zoom-in ladder**. All of that lives only in the eval proposal (`docs/visualize-eval/proposals/13/SKILL.md`), which the eval generators were pointed at. ## What already works (engine, verified)

- Three-row wrapped section descriptions
- Multi-diagram canvases with per-level titles

## What will still bite
1. **Contiguity**: a container is a rectangle, so it swallows anything inside its members' bounding box. Scattered members drag externals in. For an arbitrary component this is the main constraint — the fix is a layout feature that clusters members.
2. **Container drift** on a panned or differently-fitted pane (exact at natural fit, which is why the approval render worked).
3. **Label overwrite**: a route crossing the top edge can eat a character of the container label.
4. **No C4 element kinds**: person vs system vs container differ only by group hue; there's no boundary/actor styling.
5. **Size**: a five-level C4 is 173×128 — bigger than a pane, so it pans (zoom-out is capped at 100% by design).

args.content:
# Brief — the `c4` skill

Build a skill that produces **C4 architecture views** with the `visualize`
engine's `containers` feature, gathering its facts with scout subagents.
The reference output is the approved machine-manager diagram
(`docs/visualize-eval/rounds/14/c4-l0/`): one canvas, a level ladder,
container boxes, and three-row descriptions.

## Why a separate skill

`visualize` draws relationships from facts the caller already has. C4 adds
three things it does not do:

1. **A level ladder** — L0 system context, then L1/L1b container views,
   then L2 component views. Each level exists to motivate the next.
2. **Fact gathering** — C4 must be complete about *who calls what and
   why*. Scouts read the codebase and produce an evidence-backed element
   and relationship inventory before any spec exists.
3. **Containment** — a container box holds the component's own parts and
   nothing else. That is a claim about ownership, so it needs sources.

## Level ladder (the shape that was approved)

| Level | Draws | Box behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **L0 system context** | the component as ONE plain node, plus every actor and external system around it | no container, no double border — the point is the surrounding world |
| **L1 containers** | the component opened one level: its own deployable/runtime units inside a container, the externals from L0 outside | container on the internals |
| **L1b side view** | optional second slice when one level cannot hold the flow (e.g. the machine side of a control plane) | container, same rules |
| **L2 components** | the relationships *inside* one container | container |
| **L2b** | optional second slice of the same depth | container |

Every level carries a **description of one to three wrapped rows** (≤96
columns each) stating what is inside the box, what is outside, and how it
relates to its neighbour level. Titles stay short.

## Fact gathering — scout protocol

Before generating, gather facts. Do not invent an element or a relation.

- **Scope scout** — where the component lives: entry points, deployable
  units, data stores, external services it calls, and the actors that
  drive it. Output: element inventory with file paths.
- **Relationship scout** — for every element pair, the relation verb, the
  transport (gRPC, HTTP, SQL, queue, SSH, …) and its direction. Output:
  `from → to : verb + transport` list with sources.
- **Boundary scout** — what is INSIDE the component and what is a
  neighbour. This is the containment claim: cite the module/package or
  deployment boundary that justifies each member.
- **Level scout** (optional) — which elements belong to which C4 level,
  and why a level needs splitting into L1/L1b.

Each scout returns **evidence with file:line references**. The generator
reconciles them into one ledger; conflicts are resolved by citing the
stronger source, and unresolved conflicts are recorded, never silently
dropped.

**Completeness rule:** every element and relation a scout reports appears
in some level. If a level cannot hold it, add a level; never delete a
relation to make a diagram fit. Record a relations→level coverage map in
the generation record.

## Spec mechanics (the parts that are easy to get wrong)

- One canvas, `"direction": "lr"`, no per-diagram overrides.
- `"containers": [{"label": "...", "members": [...]}]` per diagram. The box
  is a real double-bordered rectangle grown around those members with the
  label set into the top edge.
- **Members must be contiguous.** A container is a rectangle: anything
  inside the members' bounding box is swallowed. Give a non-contiguous
  service its own `containers` entry rather than letting the box take the
  externals.
- At L0 the component is a **plain node** — no container, no `focus`.
- Descriptions: 1–3 wrapped rows, ≤96 columns, no ellipsis.
- Sizes: aim for a level inside 77×47; a larger canvas is allowed and pans,
  but zoom-out is capped at 100%, so a level that needs a wider pane than
  the tab simply pans.
- Verified at the natural fit. A container border is exact there and can
  drift on a panned pane; if a level needs panning, record it.

## Verification before claiming success

- `rataflow-view --check <spec>`: `0 near-misses`, `labels N/N, 0
  ambiguous`, `0 dot violations`, `0 crossings`.
- Inspect the render: every external outside every box, every member inside
  one, no label covered by a crossing edge, descriptions readable.
- Compare against the golden render at the same size; differences in level
  structure or coverage are defects, cosmetic differences are not.

## Deliverable

`<skill dir>/SKILL.md` plus any scout prompt files it needs. The skill is
invoked as `/c4 <component>` (or by description: "give me a C4 view of X"),
and it must work in a repository it has never seen by running its scouts
first — no prior knowledge of the component's internals.

## Acceptance test

Run the skill against **modal-machine-manager** in the `modal` repository.
The produced ladder must match the golden diagram on: level set (L0, L1,
L1b, L2, L2b), containment (which elements are members vs externals), and
relationship coverage (all 23 source relations, once each). Cosmetic
differences and level-splitting choices are acceptable when recorded.

# Rubric from the owner's own verdicts

Every criterion below is derived from a specific thing the owner said in
this session — praised or panned. Quotes are verbatim. The point is to
score what the owner actually looks at, not what a checker can count.

## A. Verdict log (what the owner said)

### A.1 Complaints

| # | Quote | Defect class |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | "the visualize skill is kinda ass… hardly readable. The lines keep overlapping with each other, have random colors, and the arrow heads are generally just awkward" | overlap; meaningless colour; arrowhead craft |
| 6 | "I don't see any colors in the diagram at all. Is that by design?" | colour must be present and intentional |
| 7 | "the iPXE arrow… seems to go down and intersect with a bunch of other arrows for effectively no reason since it comes right back up after" | pointless detour; gratuitous crossing |
| 8 | "random arrows that are not clear. The river job arrow to S3… seems to also connect to providers and janitor"; "the arrow from machines to boot server doesn't really start well" | ambiguous adjacency; bad origin attachment |
| 11 | "the borders around these cells are not actually fully in the same color… confirm whether every border is actually complete" | border integrity |
| 38 | "most of the results are worse than the previous round" | regression |
| 55 | "the rack software visualization loses a lot of the nuance of the relationships… I'm not trying to lose all of the flexibility in building deep relationships" | detail loss |
| 78 | "I don't need this subgraph structure actually shown… I almost never want them to have a border around them" | regionless grouping |
| 82 | "why couldn't the outgoing arrows from web-tier be rearranged so that there is no overlap at all"; "why is the diagram fully linear. There are multiple other connections… flat out missing"; "basically all detail from v4 is gone" | avoidable overlap; false linearity; coverage loss |
| 84 | "why is linearity the recipe. The primary goal is to express the connections… not give a very watered down version" | coverage outranks shape |
| 96 | "both the modal diagrams are worse. They lose a lot of detail" | thinning on split |
| 101 | "why are there multiple views for a single eval? previously we always only had one" | unexplained fragmentation |
| 103 | "The arrows feel a bit ambiguous… in cases where the arrows can have so many ambiguous paths, it would be good to use dots and have the dots have either the color of their src or dest, whichever leads to the least conflicts" | ambiguity escalation; dot hue binding |
| 104 | "a better learning… make sure that arrows don't overlap in a way that introduces ambiguity" | ambiguity-free routing |
| 114 | "some cases, like the home lab diagram, where the diagram stretches super wide"; "all dividers… the same size… add a divider at the top as well" | bounding-box balance; divider uniformity |
| 125 | "the top border for the entries inside machine manager is missing" | completeness of a drawn box |

### A.2 Complements

| # | Quote | What earned it |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | "this attempt… is much more organized than what we started with so that's good" | organised layout |
| 26 | "Most of the diagrams are objectively better, so I'd say this eval process is going well" | overall trajectory |
| 114 | "I mostly like all of the diagrams… They're all pretty good"; "I really like the dividers that you added" | dividers; general quality |
| 124 | "this looks good" | container box grown to hold members |
| 126 | "I like how the label is moved to the border for this case. That looks nice." | label set into the box edge |
| 128 | "The first diagram is good. It shows the machine manager and how the components fit into each other. L2 is also solid as it demonstrates the relationships inside the box. Overall I really like the diagram." | containment legibility; internal relationships |
| 131 | "this diagram is great." | the full L0→L2b ladder |
| 133 | "The skill is pretty sick now, I'm a big fan of it." | the skill as a whole |

## B. The rubric this implies

Nine categories, each with a **reader test** (what a human does) rather
than a counter. Score the render, then confirm with the check output.

### 1. `semantic_coverage` — nothing was watered down
- Every relation the source states appears, with its verb/transport text.
- **Reader test:** pick three relations from the source at random; find each
  one. If any is absent, fail. *(#55, #82, #84, #96)*
- Never fail a diagram for being dense: density is the goal, not a risk.
  *(#84, #97)*

### 2. `ambiguity_free_routing` — no path suggests a relation that is not there
- No route runs along or hugs a node that is not its endpoint.
- No route passes within 2 cells of an unrelated node unless the source
  forces it, and forced cases are named.
- No avoidable overlap between two routes; a shared corridor is a defect
  unless they are the same relation's branches. *(#7, #103, #104, #82)*
- **Reader test:** for each node, can you tell which arrows touch it? A
  human answering "that one seems to also connect to X" is a fail. *(#8)*

### 3. `arrow_craft` — attachment and shape
- Every route starts and ends at the middle of the side it leaves/enters.
- No route leaves a node, goes away, and comes back for no reason. *(#7)*
- Arrowheads are clean: no double heads, no head sitting on a bend, no head
  detached from its line. *(#0)*
- Arrowheads are flair: a diagram is not required to animate. *(#34)*

### 4. `label_ownership` — a reader can bind every label to its edge
- Each label sits unambiguously beside its own route; the checker's
  "0 ambiguous" is necessary, never sufficient. *(#8, #103)*
- Where placement cannot be unambiguous, a leader tick or a reserved
  gutter ties it down.
- **Reader test:** cover the arrows; do the labels still say which edge is
  which?

### 5. `color_meaning` — every colour says something
- No colour appears without a reason (group family, selection, dot
  binding). *(#6, #0)*
- A group tag keeps one hue across every diagram of a canvas.
- A dot's hue binds to its source or destination — whichever leaves fewer
  conflicts — once the diagram is dense enough to need it. *(#103)*
- **Reader test:** ask "what does this colour mean?" per hue; a shrug is a
  fail.

### 6. `border_integrity` — every box is whole
- Every node border is closed and one continuous colour.
- A container box is closed on all four sides and its label never loses a
  character to a crossing edge. *(#11, #125, #126)*
- Nothing is painted over a border except that border's own style.

### 7. `view_strategy` — the reader can navigate what was produced
- Rung 1: one concept fitting 77×47 → one view, side-by-side readable.
- Rung 2: multiple concepts or too large → ONE canvas of described
  diagrams. *Splitting into separate views with nothing explaining them is
  the #101/#105 defect.*
- Descriptions are mandatory on a canvas: 1–3 wrapped rows saying what is
  inside, what is outside, and how it relates to its neighbours. *(#106,
  #128)*
- **Reader test:** hand the canvas to someone who knows nothing; can they
  say what each section is for? *(#106, #108)*

### 8. `proportion` — the drawing keeps a sane shape
- Sibling sections share roughly the same bounding box; a 210×5 ribbon
  next to a 40×30 block fails. *(#114)*
- Every divider spans the widest band; the first section carries a top
  rule too. *(#114)*
- One reading direction across a canvas unless a measured reason forces
  another. *(#118)*

### 9. `containment_legibility` — C4-style zoom reads literally
- The zoom parent is visibly the box that the next level expands.
- Its contents sit INSIDE the box; actors and external systems sit OUTSIDE.
- A service that cannot be contiguous gets its own box rather than being
  left outside or swallowing externals.
- An edge crossing the boundary keeps its cells: a gap reads as
  pass-through. *(#124, #128, #131)*

## C. What the current rubric gets wrong

| Current bias | Owner's correction |
|---|---|
| Counts defects (`0 ambiguous`, `0 near-miss`) and trusts them | Four verdicts failed on things the checker scored 0 *(#8, #103, #104)* |
| Treats a split into views as neutral | A split with no description is a defect *(#101, #106)* |
| Docks density | Density is the goal; thinning is the defect *(#84, #97)* |
| Rewards fitting 77×47 | Fitting is rung 1 only; a big canvas is allowed if described *(#102, #106)* |
| Ignores aesthetics | "awkward arrow heads", "this looks nice", "this is great" are verdicts *(#0, #126, #131)* |
| Models groups as geometry | Groups are tags; no drawn regions *(#78)* |

## D. Scored anchors

Use these three as calibration, in both directions:

- **fail**: the r10 network diagram (overlapping fan, ambiguous exits) and
  the r11 modal pair ("lose a lot of detail").
- **pass**: the r14 machine-manager ladder (L0 plain box; L1/L1b/L2/L2b
  containers; three-row descriptions) — "this diagram is great."
- **pass, narrowly**: the pipeline single view — "one view… everything
  visible" — versus the r11 server canvas, which failed on source fidelity
  despite drawing well.

|---|---|
| "hardly readable… lines keep overlapping… random colors… awkward arrow heads" | overlap, colour meaning, arrow craft |
| "arrows still all over the place… iPXE goes down and comes right back up for no reason" | no pointless detours |

four scout subagents gather evidence, a prioritisation rule decides what earns a
place on the diagram, and the `visualize` engine draws it with container boxes.

A relation earns a place when it: **I1** crosses the component boundary · **I2** is a primary
request/control/data path · **I3** carries a protocol or qualifier (RPC verb, transport, port,
interval) · **I4** explains a store or actor you cannot infer · **I5** is one leg of a redundant
path that must stay countable.
It leaves only as **C1** internal detail · **C2** duplicate call site · **C3** helper that
re-enters the same container · **C4** redundant leg — and every ledger row ends as

Not our work. I checked before doing it, and **opening that PR would be harmful** — so I stopped.

## Why
`fix/visualize-skill` is already merged (squash `5e459671`). But because a squash merge leaves no ancestry link, GitHub would treat the branch as 84 *new* commits — and the branch is stale against today's `main`. A PR from it would show **7,343 files** and, if merged, **revert** work that landed after us:

```
D  agents/.agents/skills/missions/SKILL.md
D  agents/.agents/skills/professor/{artifacts,instruments,lab,learn,probe,status}.md
M  agents/.agents/skills/{mermaid,no-mistakes,professor,simple}/SKILL.md
242 files changed, 2650 insertions(+), 21750 deletions(-)
```

That's main's newer work being deleted, not ours being added.

## Everything of ours is already in main
| File | main vs local |
|---|---|
| `rataflow/src/lib.rs` | identical |
| `rataflow/src/router.rs` | identical |

| `agents/.agents/skills/c4/SKILL.md` | identical |

Even the one file that differs is fine: main carries a **better** version of my CI fix — it attributes `systemd-analyze` diagnostics to the unit that owns them, rather than my cruder substring filter. So main is ahead, not behind.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a durable, self-contained rollout record from a pi session transcript.

Keeps every owner turn verbatim, every assistant turn's prose (bounded), every
tool call with its arguments, and a bounded snippet of each tool result. Drops
thinking blocks and full tool output, which is where the megabytes live.
"""

import collections
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

SRC = Path(
    os.path.expanduser(
        "~/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-aviral-.herdr-worktrees-dotfiles-fix-visualize-skill--/"
        "2026-11-01T11-19-06-440Z_01a196d5-a5c7-768f-90ee-142b1f334f9a.jsonl"
    )
)
OUT = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/dotfiles/docs/rollouts/2026-11-01-visualize-c4-hillclimb"))
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

RESULT_SNIPPET = 400
TEXT_CAP = 4000


def blocks(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
    return [c for c in content if isinstance(c, dict)] if isinstance(content, list) else []


def clip(text, n):
    text = text or ""
    return text if len(text) <= n else text[:n] + f" …[+{len(text) - n} chars]"


turns = []
owner_turns = []
models, compactions = [], 0
tools = collections.Counter()
for line in SRC.open(encoding="utf-8"):
    try:
        rec = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    kind = rec.get("type")
    ts = rec.get("timestamp")
    if kind == "model_change":
        models.append({"ts": ts, "model": rec.get("modelId"), "provider": rec.get("provider")})
        continue
    if kind == "compaction":
        compactions += 1
        continue
    if kind != "message":
        continue
    msg = rec.get("message") or {}
    role = msg.get("role")
    text_parts, calls, result = [], [], None
    for b in blocks(msg.get("content")):
        btype = b.get("type")
        if btype == "text":
            text_parts.append(b.get("text", ""))
        elif btype == "toolCall":
            name = b.get("name") or b.get("toolName") or "?"
            tools[name] += 1
            calls.append({"tool": name, "args": b.get("arguments") or b.get("input") or b.get("args")})
        elif btype == "thinking":
            continue
    if role == "toolResult":
        result = {
            "tool": msg.get("toolName"),
            "isError": bool(msg.get("isError")),
            "chars": len("".join(text_parts)),
            "snippet": clip("".join(text_parts), RESULT_SNIPPET),
        }
    text = "\n".join(p for p in text_parts if p).strip()
    if role == "user" and text:
        if re.match(r"^(Sub-agent |The conversation history|<|# )", text):
            continue
        owner_turns.append({"ts": ts, "text": text})
    turns.append(
        {
            "ts": ts,
            "role": role,
            "text": clip(text, TEXT_CAP) if role == "assistant" else text,
            "tool_calls": calls or None,
            "tool_result": result,
        }
    )

first, last = turns[0]["ts"], turns[-1]["ts"]
digest = hashlib.sha256(SRC.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

# ---- raw-ish transcript (JSONL, one line per turn)
with (OUT / "transcript.jsonl").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for t in turns:
        fh.write(json.dumps(t, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

# ---- owner turns, verbatim and numbered
owner_md = ["# Owner turns — verbatim", "", f"{len(owner_turns)} messages, {first} → {last}", ""]
for i, t in enumerate(owner_turns, 1):
    stamp = (t["ts"] or "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
    body = t["text"].replace("\n", "\n  ")
    owner_md += [f"**{i}. `{stamp}`**", "", f"  {body}", ""]
(OUT / "owner-turns.md").write_text("\n".join(owner_md), encoding="utf-8")

# ---- assistant prose, bounded
asst = [t for t in turns if t["role"] == "assistant" and t["text"]]
asst_md = ["# Assistant turns — prose only", "", f"{len(asst)} turns, thinking dropped", ""]
for i, t in enumerate(asst, 1):
    stamp = (t["ts"] or "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
    asst_md += [f"### {i}. `{stamp}`", "", t["text"], ""]
(OUT / "assistant-turns.md").write_text("\n".join(asst_md), encoding="utf-8")

metrics = {
    "source_session": str(SRC),
    "source_sha256": digest,
    "source_bytes": SRC.stat().st_size,
    "window": {"first": first, "last": last},
    "turns": len(turns),
    "owner_turns": len(owner_turns),
    "assistant_text_turns": len(asst),
    "tool_calls": dict(tools.most_common()),
    "models": models,
    "compactions": compactions,
    "files": ["transcript.jsonl", "owner-turns.md", "assistant-turns.md", "README.md", "metrics.json"],
}
(OUT / "metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

print(json.dumps({k: metrics[k] for k in ("turns", "owner_turns", "assistant_text_turns", "compactions")}, indent=1))
print("tools:", tools.most_common(8))
print("models:", len(models), "changes;", [m["model"] for m in models[:4]])
